scenes.text: Have you ever wondered what absolute silence actually sounds like, because there is a room in Minnesota so quiet that nobody can stand staying inside for more than forty five minutes.
It is called an anechoic chamber, and because it absorbs ninety nine percent of all sound, the moment you step inside, the external world completely vanishes.
Within minutes, your ears adapt to the eerie stillness, and you start hearing things you never should, like your own lungs breathing, the rushing of blood, and even your eyeballs sliding.

Without acoustic feedback, you lose your balance and must sit down in this terrifying psychological trap, so would you dare to spend an hour here, or would you lose your mind? Tell me in the comments!
